one_month_reasoning: Window 2026-11-23 to 2026-12-20. Starting point: the stock closed $122.28 on 11-20 after an AI-sector rout (-11.7% that day, -45% in a month; Trefis, source 27) and traded ~$147 on the morning of 11-23 (+20%) after NVIDIA reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO (8-K, source 19). Scheduled: (1) Marvell Q3 FY27 results in early December: revenue is already pre-announced as consistent with the $3.15B guide (range narrowed to +/-2%, source 14), so the swing is the Q4 guide and the FY28 outlook (Investor Day ~$20B vs consensus $19.84B and our $18.5B); (2) Broadcom FQ4 results in mid-December (AI guide $21.7B for the quarter, source 20) as the custom-silicon read-across; (3) Lumentum/Marvell S-4 and any shareholder pushback on the merger (LITE CEO Hurlston: vote is a failure path, source 26); (4) the Fed in mid-December. After a -45% month and a +20% rebound day, reversal and momentum effects roughly cancel; we centre the distribution at $145 (a partial fade of the 11-23 pop) with a 25% one-month sigma (86% annual vol / 3.5), symmetric in log terms.

fair_value.method: Research target (12m) $182.58 = 0.75 x P/E leg $197.91 (25.78x after-SBC on the build's horizon NTM EPS ~$7.82, with the Celestial earnout and the Lumentum merger at expected value) + 0.25 x normalised-earnings leg $136.59 (28% mid-cycle after-SBC margin x 22.22x).

inputs_detail.derivation: FY2026 base 685 = file 2026 base 1,225 / (Big-4 2026 base 733 / Big-4 2025 actual ~410) = 1,225/1.79. Quarter split rising through each year as Big-4 run-rates did in 2026: FY27 270/295/315/345 (=1,225), FY28 420/450/470/501 (=1,841), FY29 535/555/575/590 (=2,255). No deviation from the file base: no company has given a numeric 2027 figure yet (source 16), and the newer evidence (NVIDIA Q4 guide, LightCounting's +50%) sits on it; TSMC CEO C.C. Wei's 2027 caution (source 23) is about consumer and price-sensitive markets, not AI.

inputs_detail.derivation: Q3 FY27: Marvell DC moves with NVIDIA's same-quarter DC (+21% q/q, source 18): 2,171.5 x 1.21 = 2,627.5 -> share 2,627.5/315 = 0.834% (+21% q/q vs the CEO's ">20%" Q3 statement, source 11: inside). Q4 FY27: NVIDIA's Q4 guide $130.0B / $115.8B = +12.3% (calendar-aligned merchant spend; we do not add Broadcom's +30% custom ramp) -> 2,950.7 -> 0.855%; FY27 DC 9,582 (+57%, below the CEO's ~60%). FY28: DC mix (judgment, Marvell does not disclose it) electro-optics ~50%, custom ~35%, switching/storage/other ~15% of FY27 DC; growth optics +70% (LightCounting transceivers +76% in 2027, less LPO/CPO and Broadcom share pressure), custom +90% (CEO "more than double", trimmed for the Trainium/Alchip risk), other +25% -> x1.7025 -> DC 16,313; share path 0.86/0.875/0.89/0.915% gives 16,317 (avg 0.886%). FY29: optics +40% (LightCounting growth fading), custom +60% (below Will Chu's ">$12B" FY29 custom: our custom FY29 ~10.2B), other +20% -> DC 23,754 (+46%); share 1.02/1.045/1.065/1.08% gives 23,753 (avg 1.053%). Other ways to build it: (a) Marvell's own FY28 ~$20B outlook (source 12) would put FY28 DC ~17.8B (+9%); (b) consensus FY28 revenue $19.84B (source 29) ~ DC 17.7B; (c) Broadcom-relative build: Marvell DC growing at half Broadcom's FY27 AI doubling (source 20) gives FY28 DC ~14.4B (-12%).

downside.story: 10th percentile: AI capex 22% below the base path (toward the standing file's low case: 2027 $1,390B, 2028 $1,265B) as the November AI selloff turns into budget cuts at labs and neoclouds; Marvell loses custom share (Trainium/Alchip, an XPU program slips) and module makers move DSP sockets to Broadcom/Credo after the Lumentum deal (Counterpoint): share -10%; GM -1.5pt on deleverage; P/E -6 turns on the after-SBC basis (~19.8x, ~16x on the peers' basis, at the CRDO/COHR end of today's peer range). Deal still pending with an overpaid LITE at peak optics.

base.story: Median: AI capex on the standing file's base path (CY26 $1,225B -> CY27 $1,841B -> CY28 $2,255B); Marvell DC share 0.78% -> 0.89% -> 1.05% from 1.6T DSP and custom ramps read across from NVIDIA, Broadcom and LightCounting; FY28 revenue $18.5B (7% below the ~$20B outlook and the $19.84B consensus), FY29 $26.0B; 25.78x after-SBC NTM P/E on post-selloff peer multiples; Lumentum merger pending at the horizon, p 0.70, costing about $2.9 a share at expected value (LITE valued on its own forward EPS is worth a little less than the 453.7M shares issued).

upside.story: 90th percentile: AI capex near the file's high path (2027 ~$2.2T) as the Q4 calls put numbers on "significantly more" 2027 spend; Marvell reaches the Investor Day FY28 ~$20B and FY29 custom >$12B with 1.6T DSPs and scale-up optics (share +8%); GM +0.5pt; peer multiples recover from the November rout (+6 turns after SBC). The deal closes on schedule with laser-supply and $1B+ cost synergies and no material DSP customer loss.

Peers' ex-SBC forward P/E converted to after-SBC with the build's own horizon NTM ratio 1.234. Share count moves only by buybacks (-0.5%/yr), so SBC issuance is not counted again. FY26 SBC 590.8 (F36), TTM 828.9 (F39).

reasoning: Fresh run on 2026-11-23 in the industry lane. What changed since the October set: Marvell signed an all-stock merger with Lumentum on 2026-11-02 (4.500 ratio, ~33% to LITE holders, close 1H CY2028, sources 13-14) and pre-announced Q3 revenue consistent with its $3.15B guide; the stock fell ~45% in a month through an AI-wide selloff (NVIDIA -14%, AVGO -12% on 11-20; Trefis 27-28) and NVIDIA's CEO removal, then bounced ~20% on 11-23 when Huang was reinstated (19). Driver build: DC revenue = customer AI capex (standing file base, unchanged: no numeric 2027 company guide yet; Q3 calls say "significantly"/"meaningfully more", source 16; LightCounting also assumes +50% capex in 2027, 17) x Marvell share. The share path is built from the rest of the chain: Q3 DC tracks NVIDIA's +21% q/q (18), Q4 its +12.3% guide, FY28 from a mix of optics +70% (LightCounting transceivers +76%), custom +90% (CEO "more than double", trimmed for Alchip/Trainium) and other +25%; FY29 optics +40%, custom +60%. Result: FY27 revenue 11,762 (2.0% under the ~$12B outlook), FY28 18,452 (7% under the ~$20B outlook and the $19.84B consensus), FY29 25,962; non-GAAP GM 58.3/57.4/56.5% (CFO: FY28 similar to 2H FY27); opex at half the revenue growth (CFO). Valuation: peer forward P/Es re-sourced from current StockAnalysis pages (the run's peers.md snapshot is 2026-10-30 and pre-selloff): median 18.0x on 8 peers, own 21.68x, k 0.8 -> 20.89x ex-SBC -> 25.78x after SBC on our NTM EPS, weight 0.75; normalised leg 0.25. Lumentum: pending at the horizon, so it enters as p 0.70 x V where V compares LITE valued on its own forward EPS (x1.45 growth, 18.4x) plus net synergies with the 453.7M shares issued at our standalone value; at our inputs it is near neutral (-2.86 a share), the downside case carries an overpaying outcome. Research target (12m) $182.58, downside $75.80 (P10: capex -22%, share -10%, GM -1.5pt, -6 turns), upside $311.55 (P90). FCF-yield leg left out (trailing peer yields on hypergrowth peers; gap_note). Research: ~30 searches/fetches; X/Twitter not used.

drivers.label: Customer AI data-center capex (ex-China, all customer groups), calendar quarter nearest the Marvell fiscal quarter

Checked against newer primary evidence dated after the file: Q3-26 calls (source 16: Alphabet CFO Ashkenazi "increase significantly in 2027", Amazon CEO Jassy "meaningfully more in 2027", Microsoft CFO Hood CY26 ~$170B with acceleration in H2 FY27, Meta CFO Li $135-145B 2026) - Big-4 2026 ~$730B, in line with the file's $733B; NVIDIA Q3 FY27 DC +21% q/q and Q4 guide $130B (+12% q/q, source 18); LightCounting assumes +50% capex in 2027 (source 17), the same +50% the file base implies (1,841/1,225).
drivers.derivation: FY2026 base 685 = file 2026 base 1,225 / (Big-4 2026 base 733 / Big-4 2025 actual ~410) = 1,225/1.79. Quarter split rising through each year as Big-4 run-rates did in 2026: FY27 270/295/315/345 (=1,225), FY28 420/450/470/501 (=1,841), FY29 535/555/575/590 (=2,255). No deviation from the file base: no company has given a numeric 2027 figure yet (source 16), and the newer evidence (NVIDIA Q4 guide, LightCounting's +50%) sits on it; TSMC CEO C.C. Wei's 2027 caution (source 23) is about consumer and price-sensitive markets, not AI.
drivers.why: Customer AI data-center spend is the economic driver of ~80-90% of Marvell revenue (custom XPUs, optical DSPs, switching).
drivers.flag: FY2026 base capex (685) is a derived estimate, low confidence; it only calibrates the base-year share, the projected years use the file's base case.

Forecast from industry read-across: NVIDIA Q3 FY27 DC +21% q/q and Q4 guide +12.3% q/q (source 18), Broadcom AI +30% q/q into its Q4 and FY27 AI ~ $115B (Hock Tan, source 20), LightCounting Ethernet transceivers +76% in 2027 and fading toward +20% by 2031 (source 17), Lumentum/Coherent capacity and guides (sources 21, 22), and Marvell's own segment commentary (sources 11, 12) as a cross-check.
drivers.derivation: Q3 FY27: Marvell DC moves with NVIDIA's same-quarter DC (+21% q/q, source 18): 2,171.5 x 1.21 = 2,627.5 -> share 2,627.5/315 = 0.834% (+21% q/q vs the CEO's ">20%" Q3 statement, source 11: inside). Q4 FY27: NVIDIA's Q4 guide $130.0B / $115.8B = +12.3% (calendar-aligned merchant spend; we do not add Broadcom's +30% custom ramp) -> 2,950.7 -> 0.855%; FY27 DC 9,582 (+57%, below the CEO's ~60%). FY28: DC mix (judgment, Marvell does not disclose it) electro-optics ~50%, custom ~35%, switching/storage/other ~15% of FY27 DC; growth optics +70% (LightCounting transceivers +76% in 2027, less LPO/CPO and Broadcom share pressure), custom +90% (CEO "more than double", trimmed for the Trainium/Alchip risk), other +25% -> x1.7025 -> DC 16,313; share path 0.86/0.875/0.89/0.915% gives 16,317 (avg 0.886%). FY29: optics +40% (LightCounting growth fading), custom +60% (below Will Chu's ">$12B" FY29 custom: our custom FY29 ~10.2B), other +20% -> DC 23,754 (+46%); share 1.02/1.045/1.065/1.08% gives 23,753 (avg 1.053%). downside.story: 10th percentile: AI capex 22% below the base path (toward the standing file's low case: 2027 $1,390B, 2028 $1,265B) as the November AI selloff turns into budget cuts at labs and neoclouds; Marvell loses custom share (Trainium/Alchip, an XPU program slips) and module makers move DSP sockets to Broadcom/Credo after the Lumentum deal (Counterpoint): share -10%; GM -1.5pt on deleverage; P/E -6 turns on the after-SBC basis (~19.8x, ~16x on the peers' basis, at the CRDO/COHR end of today's peer range). Deal still pending with an overpaid LITE at peak optics.

upside.story: 90th percentile: AI capex near the file's high path (2027 ~$2.2T) as the Q4 calls put numbers on "significantly more" 2027 spend; Marvell reaches the Investor Day FY28 ~$20B and FY29 custom >$12B with 1.6T DSPs and scale-up optics (share +8%); GM +0.5pt; peer multiples recover from the November rout (+6 turns after SBC). The deal closes on schedule with laser-supply and $1B+ cost synergies and no material DSP customer loss.

model_inputs.structure_note: Quarterly driver-led set. Value is carried by a P/E horizon leg (weight 0.75) on the build's own after-SBC NTM EPS (Q4 FY28 + Q1-Q3 FY29) and a normalised-earnings custom leg (0.25; 28% after-SBC mid-cycle margin x the peer-median multiple), per the semis playbook. Data Center revenue = customer AI capex (standing file base) x Marvell's share of it, the share built from industry read-across (NVIDIA, Broadcom, LightCounting, Lumentum/Coherent); communications a plain quarterly path; non-GAAP GM and opex drive EBIT; SBC = 0.5 x non-GAAP opex (Q1-Q2 FY27 0.36/0.53) subtracted (cost basis). Segment "ebit" is gross profit allocated by revenue (Marvell reports one segment); opex + SBC sit in corporate_ebit. Adjustments: Celestial earnout (-749.5, p 1) and the pending Lumentum merger at expected value (V, p 0.70), both deducted by hand inside the normalised leg. No DCF leg (policy). Driven share of revenue: 100%. The normalised leg is not driver-linked.
model_inputs.gap_note: For Kilian: (1) FCF-yield leg departs from the tech rule (0% instead of 40% of the P/E weight): the only peer FCF yields available are trailing (StockAnalysis TTM, median 1.49%, COHR negative) on peers growing 50-130%, so applying them to our horizon FCF would value MRVL at roughly $300+, ~+60% over the P/E leg; a forward peer FCF series is needed before the leg is meaningful (card if you want it in). (2) Lumentum merger at p 0.70 with V from LITE valued on its own forward EPS x 18.4x and a +$0.2B net synergy (+$7.8B cost synergies at 50% realisation, -$1.0B integration, -$6.6B DSP-customer dis-synergy); at LITE +25% (peak optics) V falls ~-$13B (-$10 a share at p 0.7). (3) The 28% mid-cycle margin and 0.5 opex elasticity after FY28 are judgment. (4) No financing event >= 20%: the deal is all-stock; the Google warrant (58.97M at $206.58) is out of the money at our base. (5) Peer multiples are taken after the November AI selloff (pages dated 2026-11-07 to 11-22, the latter after the 11-20 rout): on the 2026-10-30 peers.md snapshot (median ~30x) the target would be ~60% higher; we use the current pages because the timeliness rule requires them.
